title: Questioned Purchases and Retailer Refunds on the Healthy Options Card
content:
A member who does not recognise a purchase on their card, or who returned what they bought, may have it looked into and the money put back. This is the adjudication basis for purchases on a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card.

**The window.** The member raises the dispute no later than the last day of the dispute window counted from the date the purchase posted to the card, the window being the calendar days the tier carries. Calendar days are counted from the day after the posting date, every day of the week counts, a dispute raised on the final day of the window is in time, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days. The posting date is read from the card's own entry for the purchase being questioned.

*Boundary cases.* On a tier whose window is 60 calendar days, a dispute raised on the 60th day counted from the day after the purchase posted is in time; one raised on the 61st is out of time. Where a member telephones on the boundary day, the day itself counts in their favour.

**No second credit for the same purchase.** No credit against that same purchase is already posted on this programme. The card's own entries are read for a credit already standing against the purchase concerned before a further credit is put on.

**Who says what, and what decides it.** Only the member may say that a purchase was not theirs, and their statement is what opens the enquiry; but the money goes back on the card on the plan's finding, never on the statement alone.

**The provisional credit.** A provisional credit is put on the card inside the tier's provisional credit days while the enquiry runs, so the member is not left without their allowance, and it is taken back if the purchase turns out to have been theirs.

**Settlement.** The plan settles a disputed purchase inside the tier's resolution days and tells the member the outcome in writing whichever way it goes.

**A retailer's own refund.** A retailer's own refund for a returned item is not a dispute: it posts on its own when the retailer sends it, inside the tier's refund posting days, and it names the purchase it reverses.

**Where the money goes.** A refund always goes back to the card it was spent from and into the benefit period the purchase belonged to, so that a refund near a period end does not quietly become a fresh allowance.
